correctness.rationale: The proof divides deletions into whether the apex survives and counts original versus shadow deletions. Replacing a deleted original by its shadow yields a residual odd cycle unless the same shadow is deleted; if two deleted originals are nonadjacent, simultaneous shadow substitution produces an odd cycle. If the apex survives, all shadows have fixed opposite color; the flexible-original vertex-cover obstruction excludes 1- and 2-original deletion patterns, leaving exactly five n=5 exceptions. A distinct proof identifies all exchange adjacencies and exact pair distances. Two independent bipartiteness algorithms exhaustively agree on every deletion set of size at most 3 for odd n=3..25; independently built exchange graph and analytic templates agree for n=5,7,9,11,13. Finite checks support but do not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: All optimum vertex bipartization sets of a canonical infinite family of 4-chromatic triangle-free graphs are classified rather than just giving an elementary minimum. Single-exchange flexibility is nontrivial and structurally transparent: a triangularly decorated odd cycle for all n>=7, and a Petersen core at the exceptional n=5. Exact distance distributions and a geometric transition enable meaningful optima-reconfiguration comparisons; this is a natural full classification, not an arbitrary finite slice.
